{{more footnotes needed|date=May 2025}}
In mathematics, especially in differential and algebraic geometries, an '''inertia stack''' of a [[groupoid]] ''X'' is a [[stack (mathematics)|stack]] that parametrizes automorphism groups on <math>X</math> and transitions between them. It is commonly denoted as <math>\Lambda X</math> and is defined as inertia groupoids as charts. The notion often appears in particular as an '''inertia orbifold'''.

== Inertia groupoid ==
Let <math>U = (U_1 \rightrightarrows U_0)</math> be a groupoid. Then the '''inertia groupoid''' <math>\Lambda U</math> is a groupoid (= a category whose morphisms are all invertible) where
*the objects are the automorphism groups: <math>\operatorname{Aut}(x), x \in U_0,</math>
*the morphisms from ''x'' to ''y'' are conjugations by invertible morphisms <math>f : x \to y</math>; that is, an automorphism <math>g : x \to x</math> is sent to <math>f \circ g \circ f^{-1} : y \to y,</math>
*the composition is that of morphisms in <math>U</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Adem|Ruan|Zhang|2008|loc=Definition 2.6.}}</ref>

For example, if ''U'' is a [[fundamental groupoid]], then <math>\Lambda U</math> keeps track of the changes of base points.
